rubrics_metrics.name: Municipal District of Acadia No. 241 — Tax arrears payment deadline
rubrics_metrics.description: Notice is hereby given that if all arrears of taxes imposed in 1927, in respect of any parcel of land situated within this municipality are not paid on or before the first day of July next, such land will be dealt with under the provisions of The Tax Recovery Act, 1922, with a view to obtaining certificate of title in the name of the municipality in respect of such parcel.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Dated at Acadia Valley, Alta., this 23rd day of May, A.D. 1928. D. M. GRAHAM, Secretary-Treasurer M.D. No. 241. (Procedural requirement: pay 1927 arrears by July 1 to avoid municipal tax recovery proceedings.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Province of Alberta — Improvement Districts tax arrears notice
rubrics_metrics.description: NOTICE is hereby given that unless all arrears of taxes imposed in respect of any parcel of land situated in Improvement Districts Nos. 182, 211, 212, 213 in the Province of Alberta, are paid on or before the First day of July next, such land will be dealt with under the provisions of the Tax Recovery Act being Chapter 122, Revised Statutes of Alberta, 1922 with a view to obtaining Certificate of Title in the name of the Crown in the right of the Province of Alberta in respect to such parcel.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: W. D. Spence, DEPUTY MINISTER, EDMONTON, May 30th, 1928. (Procedural requirement: payment deadline and consequence specified.)

rubrics_metrics.name: How to Go Broke — Rule 1: Grow only one crop
rubrics_metrics.guidance: From the University of Tennessee extension 'How to Go Broke Farming' satirical ten rules. (Advice framed as 'do this if you want to go broke'; implied agricultural-quality criterion: avoid monoculture if you want farm resilience.)

rubrics_metrics.name: How to Go Broke — Rule 2: Keep no livestock
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part of the same ten-rule satirical list advising farmers what NOT to do if they wish to prosper.

rubrics_metrics.name: How to Go Broke — Rule 3: Regard chickens and a yard as nuisances
rubrics_metrics.description: 3. Regard chickens and a yard as nuisances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Satirical rule implying that treating small farm enterprises as nuisances is a recipe for failure.

rubrics_metrics.name: How to Go Broke — Rule 4: Take everything from the soil and return nothing
rubrics_metrics.description: 4. Take everything from the soil and return nothing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Warns implicitly that failure to replenish soil nutrients will bankrupt a farm.

rubrics_metrics.name: How to Go Broke — Rule 5: Don't stop gullies or grow top soil
rubrics_metrics.description: 5. Don't stop gullies or grow top soil; let the wash away, then you will have 'bottom' land.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Satirical admonition showing soil conservation is necessary; described as a rule to assure ruin.

rubrics_metrics.name: How to Go Broke — Rule 6: Don't plan operations; trust to luck
rubrics_metrics.description: 6. Don't plan your farm operations, It's hard work thinking—trust to luck.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Critique of lack of planning as a cause of farm failure; included to show the opposite (plan) is good practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: How to Go Broke — Rule 7: Exploit woodland as a coal mine
rubrics_metrics.description: 7. Regard your woodland as you would a coal mine, cut every tree, sell the timber and wear the cleared land out.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Satirical rule warning against deforestation and short-term exploitation of assets.

rubrics_metrics.name: How to Go Broke — Rule 8: Rely on grandfather's methods
rubrics_metrics.description: 8. Hold fast to the idea that the methods employed by your grandfather are good enough for you.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implicit criterion: resist innovation at your peril; encourages adoption of improved practices instead.

rubrics_metrics.name: How to Go Broke — Rule 9: Avoid cooperation with neighbors
rubrics_metrics.description: 9. Be independent—don't join with your neighbors in any form of co-operation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Satirical criticism of isolationism; implies that cooperation is beneficial for farmers.

rubrics_metrics.name: How to Go Broke — Rule 10: Mortgage the farm for consumables
rubrics_metrics.description: 10. Mortgage your farm for every dollar it will stand to buy things you would have the cash to buy if you followed a good system of farming.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Warns that over-leveraging for short-term consumption instead of sound farming practices leads to ruin.

rubrics_metrics.name: Queen Georgia's Cake — recipe and bake instructions
rubrics_metrics.description: Queen Georgia's Cake ingredients and method: '1 cup shortening, 1 1/2 cups sugar, 3 beaten egg yolks and 1 white (save remaining whites for frosting), 1 cup raisin juice, 1 cup sour milk, 1 cup raisins, 3 cups flour, 4 teaspoons baking powder, 1 teaspoon soda, 1 teaspoon salt, 1 teaspoon nutmeg, 1 teaspoon cloves, 1 teaspoon cinnamon; Mix and pour into 3 greased layer cake pans and bake 15 minutes in a moderate oven (350 degrees F. indicated elsewhere). Frost with boiled frosting.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedural culinary guideline — ingredient proportions, mixing order, pan arrangement, baking time and temperature cues included as production-standard for the cake.

rubrics_metrics.name: June Wedding Salad — assembly guideline
rubrics_metrics.description: June Wedding Salad: 'Cover individual salad plates with crisp leaves of head lettuce. Place on these strips of fresh or canned pineapple, one-inch squares of orange pulp cut thick, and a few smaller sections of sweetened grapefruit pulp. Top with a mound of flavored whipped cream and a maraschino or strawberry. Just before serving add a little lemon sauce—juice of one lemon mixed with two tablespoons granulated or powdered sugar.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedural recipe/instruction for assembling a wedding salad suitable for a company dinner; gives composition and serving sequence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Five Reasons — support the Wheat Pool (Reason 1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reason 1 (as printed): 'Because ... self protection as a producer is incomplete ... private organizations may still exploit ...' (header: 'FIVE REASONS WHY WHEAT PRODUCERS SHOULD SUPPORT THE WHEAT POOL')
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Promotional/cooperative principle: individual producer protection is incomplete without collective organization — avoid exploitation by private middlemen. (Text on page is partially garbled; preserves original phrasing fragments.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Five Reasons — support the Wheat Pool (Reason 2)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reason 2 (as printed): 'Because ... you by ... living by ...' (fragmentary in scan)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part of enumerated reasons urging support for the Wheat Pool; intended to argue living standards and economic security are improved by pooling. (Fragmentary original wording retained.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Five Reasons — support the Wheat Pool (Reason 3)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reason 3 (as printed): 'Because co-operation eliminates unnecessary middle-men and dividend hunting shareholders, who take a heavy toll of the wealth produced by the farm workers.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Argument that cooperative marketing reduces intermediary costs and shareholder extraction, improving producer returns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Five Reasons — support the Wheat Pool (Reason 4)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reason 4 (as printed): 'Because ... the co-operative is the principle of "each for all, all for each" which alone can bring peace and prosperity to all.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Philosophical/economic justification: co-operative principle promotes social and economic justice for producers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Five Reasons — support the Wheat Pool (Reason 5)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reason 5 (as printed): 'Because resources in co-operation instead of supporting capitalistic organizations hostile to "co-operative movements."'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Argument encouraging producers to pool resources to avoid supporting outside capitalistic interests that may be hostile to co-operative efforts.
